content: A former spouse sought the division of an apartment and cellar acquired during a marriage under the legal community regime. The Court declared the claim inadmissible because the plaintiff failed to provide a complete 20-year historical title search (certificazione ipocatastale). The Court established that this documentation is an indispensable condition for the action, as it allows the judge to verify the actual ownership of the parties and ensure the continuity of transcriptions to protect third parties. Furthermore, the ruling clarified that a Court-Appointed Expert (CTU) cannot be used to bypass procedural deadlines or to acquire documents that were within the parties' reach.
